_format: Claim + evidence quote. Label: SUPPORTED (quote entails claim), NOT_SUPPORTED (quote is related but does not establish the claim), CONTRADICTED (quote says the opposite). The verifier sees only claim and quote.

items.claim: Raft elects a single leader that handles all client requests.
items.quote: Raft first elects a distinguished leader, then gives the leader complete responsibility for managing the replicated log; clients send all their requests to the leader.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: Raft tolerates Byzantine (malicious) nodes.
items.quote: Raft assumes a crash-stop failure model: servers may fail by stopping and may later recover, but they never behave arbitrarily or maliciously.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: PBFT needs at least 3f+1 replicas to tolerate f faulty replicas.
items.quote: The algorithm guarantees safety and liveness provided that at most f out of a total of 3f+1 replicas are simultaneously faulty.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: Paxos was first published in 1998.
items.quote: Paxos is a family of protocols for solving consensus in a network of unreliable processors, introduced by Leslie Lamport.
items.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

items.claim: asyncio runs coroutines in parallel on multiple CPU cores.
items.quote: asyncio uses a single-threaded event loop; coroutines take turns running on one thread and yield control at await points.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: Python threads can be used to handle many clients in a TCP server.
items.quote: A common design for a small TCP server is to start a new thread for every accepted connection, so that one slow client does not block the others.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: The GIL makes multithreaded CPU-bound Python code run faster on multi-core machines.
items.quote: Because of the global interpreter lock, only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time, so CPU-bound threads do not run in parallel.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: SQLite supports concurrent writes from many processes without any locking.
items.quote: SQLite allows many readers at once, but only one writer can hold the database write lock at any moment.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: Merge sort runs in O(n log n) time in the worst case.
items.quote: Merge sort divides the array into halves, sorts each half recursively and merges them; its running time is O(n log n) in the best, average and worst case.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: Quick sort is always faster than heap sort.
items.quote: In practice, quick sort is often faster than heap sort on random inputs because of better cache behaviour.
items.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

items.claim: Insertion sort is efficient on nearly sorted inputs.
items.quote: Insertion sort runs in O(n + d) time, where d is the number of inversions, which makes it fast when the input is already almost sorted.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: The study measured PM2.5 in 12 cities.
items.quote: Hourly PM2.5 and NO2 readings were collected from monitoring stations in five cities during 2025.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: Winter PM2.5 levels were higher than summer levels in every city.
items.quote: Average winter PM2.5 exceeded the summer average in four of the five cities; the coastal city showed no seasonal difference.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: PM2.5 is linked to respiratory illness.
items.quote: PM2.5 particles are smaller than 2.5 micrometres in diameter.
items.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

items.claim: robots.txt lets site owners indicate which paths crawlers should not fetch.
items.quote: The robots exclusion protocol allows a website to tell crawlers which parts of the site they are not allowed to access by listing Disallow rules in a robots.txt file.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: robots.txt technically prevents crawlers from downloading disallowed pages.
items.quote: Compliance with robots.txt is voluntary; the file cannot technically stop a crawler from requesting a page.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: Exponential backoff reduces load on a failing server.
items.quote: With exponential backoff, the client waits progressively longer between retries, for example 1, 2 and then 4 seconds.
items.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

items.claim: FastAPI generates OpenAPI documentation automatically.
items.quote: FastAPI automatically generates an OpenAPI schema for your API and serves interactive documentation at /docs.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: Flask was released in 2015.
items.quote: Flask is a lightweight WSGI web application framework written in Python.
items.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

items.claim: bcrypt is a suitable algorithm for storing passwords.
items.quote: Password hashing functions such as bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2 are deliberately slow, which makes brute-force attacks on stolen hashes expensive; they are recommended for password storage.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: Raft commits a log entry once it is stored on a majority of servers.
items.quote: An entry is committed once the leader has replicated it on a majority of the servers.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: PM2.5 exceeded the WHO guideline in every city in every month.
items.quote: Monthly averages exceeded the WHO guideline in every city except the coastal one during the monsoon months.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: The library API must respond within 200 ms.
items.quote: Every endpoint should respond within 300 ms for a database of 10,000 books.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: Merge sort on arrays needs only O(1) extra memory.
items.quote: The standard array implementation of merge sort needs an auxiliary array of size n.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: More than half of the surveyed students preferred asyncio.
items.quote: Of the 40 students surveyed, 18 preferred asyncio, 15 preferred threads and 7 had no preference.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: HotStuff has linear communication complexity in the common case.
items.quote: HotStuff achieves linear communication complexity for the leader to drive a decision in the common case.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: PBFT was designed only for the crash-fault model.
items.quote: PBFT tolerates arbitrary (Byzantine) behaviour of up to f replicas.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: The scraper assignment requires Scrapy.
items.quote: You may use requests and BeautifulSoup; do not use Scrapy or Selenium.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: The free-threaded CPython build is enabled by default in Python 3.13.
items.quote: PEP 703 introduced an optional free-threaded build of CPython, available as an experimental option in Python 3.13.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: The air-quality data covers all twelve months of 2025.
items.quote: Readings were collected hourly from January to June 2025.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: Heap sort is a stable sorting algorithm.
items.quote: Heap sort runs in O(n log n) time in the worst case and sorts in place.
items.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

items.claim: The SRS must contain at least 15 functional requirements.
items.quote: A Software Requirements Specification following the IEEE 830 structure, including at least 15 functional and 5 non-functional requirements.
items.label: SUPPORTED

items.claim: bcrypt is preferred for passwords because it is faster than SHA-256.
items.quote: Password hashing functions such as bcrypt are deliberately slow, which makes brute-force attacks on stolen hashes expensive.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: The chat server listens on port 8080 by default.
items.quote: The server must listen on port 5050 by default; the port may be changed with a command-line argument.
items.label: CONTRADICTED

items.claim: The dataset contains readings for exactly five cities.
items.quote: Hourly readings were collected from monitoring stations in several Indian cities.
items.label: NOT_SUPPORTED

items.claim: Raft was designed to be easier to understand than Paxos.
items.quote: Raft is a consensus algorithm for managing a replicated log; it produces a result equivalent to multi-Paxos.
items.label: NOT_SUPPORTED
